For minimizing text duplication in your HTML project with minimal programming, here are some practical approaches:

## 1. **CSS Variables for Repeated Text Content**
You can use CSS `content` property with custom properties for short, repeated text:


```css
:root {
    --check-in-time: "od 15:00";
    --check-out-time: "do 10:00";
}

.check-in::after {
    content: var(--check-in-time);
}
```


## 2. **HTML Data Attributes + CSS**
Store text in one place and reference it:


```html
<div data-text="Jindřichův dům" class="title"></div>
```


## 3. **Use HTML Templates**
The `<template>` tag lets you define reusable HTML blocks without duplication.

## 4. **Simple JavaScript Approach (Minimal)**
Add a small script at the end of your HTML:


```html
<script>
const texts = {
    wifi_name: "jindrichuvdum_hoste",
    wifi_password: "Jindrich",
    phone: "739 655 826"
};

// Replace placeholders like {{wifi_name}}
document.body.innerHTML = document.body.innerHTML.replace(
    /\{\{(\w+)\}\}/g, 
    (_, key) => texts[key] || ''
);
</script>
```


## 5. **Use Emmet Snippets in VS Code**

Create reusable code snippets for frequently used HTML blocks:



Select "html.json" and add your snippets for common text blocks.

## 6. **Consider a Static Site Generator**
For a no/low-code solution, tools like **Eleventy** or **Hugo** let you use simple templating with data files (JSON/YAML) without much programming knowledge.

The simplest approach for your current file would be **option 4** (JavaScript variables) or **option 5** (VS Code snippets for authoring).
